question: While building your customer support resolution agent, you use Claude Code to trace why the agent calls escalate_to_human for simple refunds that process_refund could handle. You named that Claude Code session refund-escalation-trace. Two days later you return to the work, and nobody has changed the agent's code or prompts since then. How should you continue that specific investigation?

options.text: Run Claude Code with the -p flag and the prompt refund-escalation-trace so that it continues the earlier investigation non-interactively.
options.reason: The -p flag runs Claude Code in non-interactive mode with a new prompt; it does not resume a named session, so the earlier context is lost.

options.text: Run Claude Code with --resume refund-escalation-trace so that the named session continues with its earlier context.
options.reason: Named session resumption with --resume <session-name> continues a specific prior conversation, and the earlier context is still valid because nothing has changed.

options.text: Open a new Claude Code session and run /compact so that it rebuilds the context of the refund-escalation-trace conversation.
options.reason: /compact reduces context usage inside the current session; it does not bring back the conversation of an earlier named session.

options.text: Open a new Claude Code session and run /memory to load the refund-escalation-trace conversation from the project memory files.
options.reason: /memory deals with the CLAUDE.md memory files that are loaded; it does not load an earlier session's conversation, which only --resume continues.
